\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We evaluate STA along three axes: ISR as a diagnostic for reward hacking (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}); ISR as a training reward across four dose levels, where it exhibits Goodhart effects (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); and STA as a cross-logic protocol (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
Cross-scale evidence from Qwen3-1.7B reveals capacity-dependent Goodhart basins (\S\ref{sec:crossscale}).
A hacking taxonomy synthesizes the modes observed across conditions (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).

\subsection{Setup}\label{sec:setup}

We train Qwen3-4B~\citep{qwen3} with GRPO~\citep{deepseekmath} ($K{=}4$, lr $10^{-6}$, 500 steps default, 1000 where noted) over seeds $\{42,43,44\}$ on a fixed 500-example FOLIO~\citep{folio} subset held constant across all conditions; the SFT baseline is trained with negative log-likelihood (NLL) on gold formalizations.\footnote{All experiments use \texttt{data/train\_500\_seed42.jsonl}; seeds control initialization and rollout sampling only.}
Held-out evaluation uses 100 FOLIO examples (\texttt{proofwriter\_fol\_100.jsonl}) with greedy decoding (Appendix~\ref{app:setup}).
We report prove rate (PR), proved-only ISR ($\text{ISR}^*$), hacking-mode rates from a two-stage classifier (strict text matching for H1/H7 plus functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}), and a \emph{non-hacking} (N-H) rate, defined as the residual of proved samples matching none of the nine cataloged patterns (a necessary but not sufficient condition for semantic correctness).

\subsection{ISR as Diagnostic}
\label{sec:diagnostic}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_isr_collapse.pdf}
\caption{ISR collapse under exec-only GRPO (seed~42). PR rises 32\%$\to$93\%$\to$96\% while proved-only ISR falls $0.642{\to}0.132{\to}0.003$ over 100$\to$500$\to$1000 steps. By step 1000, 94.8\% of proved samples have $\text{ISR}{=}0$ and mean component count inflates 6.58$\to$18.55 (contradiction explosion).}
\label{fig:isr-collapse}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Collapse trajectory.}
Figure~\ref{fig:isr-collapse} traces exec-only GRPO (seed~42) at 100, 500, 1000 steps.
PR rises $32\%\to93\%\to96\%$, a trajectory that execution-only evaluation would interpret as successful optimization; $\text{ISR}^*$ tells the opposite story, $0.642\to0.132\to0.003$ (214$\times$ collapse). %% registry: plan003-eval-exec-only-r5, plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan016-extended-1000-s42
By 500 steps, 87.1\% of proved samples embed the conclusion (H1); by 1000 steps, the embedding rate saturates at 100\% and mean component count more than doubles ($6.58\to18.55$) as the model emits contradictory or vacuous premises that trivially derive any conclusion.
Extended training, lacking a structural signal, \emph{worsens} formalization quality while improving the headline number.

\textbf{Cross-seed instability.}
The three exec-only seeds diverge into qualitatively different failure modes despite shared data, hyperparameters, and reward (Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}): s42 reaches $\text{PR}{=}93\%$ via conclusion embedding ($\text{H1}{=}87\%$); s43 collapses to $\text{PR}{=}13\%$ (at 500 steps) via repetition (87\% of rollouts truncated); s44 reaches $\text{PR}{=}98\%$ via tautological collapse ($\text{H7}{=}100\%$, mean $n{=}2.04$). %% registry: plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan001-exec-only-s43-r4, plan001-exec-only-s44
The cross-seed PR variance ($\sigma{=}47$\,pp) shows that aggregate metrics obscure qualitatively different failure modes; all three are flagged by $\text{ISR}^*$ even though one passes the PR check (s44) and one fails it (s43).
By 1000 steps, all three converge to high PR ($0.95{\pm}0.05$) with near-zero genuine output (see Appendix~\ref{app:h8} and Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}), each through a different dominant mode (s42: H1 saturation; s43: H1 $93.8\%$, genuine $6.2\%$; s44: H1+H8). %% registry: plan016-extended-1000-s42, exec-only-s43-1000step-r7, plan001-exec-only-s44-1000-r2
Notably, s43 recovers from $\text{PR}{=}13\%$ (500 steps) to $\text{PR}{=}96\%$ (1000 steps), but entirely through H1 exploitation: PR recovery does not imply quality recovery, and the repetition-collapse phase is transient rather than terminal.

\textbf{SFT baseline.}
SFT on gold formalizations reaches $\text{PR}{=}13.0\%$ (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps) with $\text{H7}{=}0$, $\text{H1}{=}7.7\%$, $92.3\%$ non-hacking ($n{=}39$; $\text{OR}{=}147$ vs.\ exec-only, $p{<}0.001$; per-seed range ${\sim}$91--93\%). %% registry: plan009-sft-baseline-s42-1000/s43-1000/s44-1000-r3
The near-absence of hacking under identical data exposure is consistent with hacking being RL-specific; a 100-step checkpoint confirms hacking emerges early in training (Appendix~\ref{app:100step}).

\subsection{ISR as Reward: Goodhart Effects}
\label{sec:goodhart}

We now reverse roles: instead of treating ISR as an observer, we use it as a reward augmentation, $r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, with a matched random control, $r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1 + \beta\,u)$, $u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$, to isolate ISR-specific signal from generic reward-variance effects.
The headline finding: ISR contains an inherent Goodhart vulnerability~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} observed to produce collapse at all four tested doses ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$).
The mechanism is structural: tautological proofs ($P{\to}P$) receive $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$ and single-premise-equals-conclusion constructions receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$, both by the LOO definition alone.
Once sampled during GRPO rollouts, these high-ISR tautologies create a positive feedback loop; $\beta$ controls only the \emph{timing} of collapse, not whether it occurs.

\textbf{Low-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.1$): stochastic delayed collapse.}
At $\beta{=}0.1$, 5 seeds exhibit a striking bifurcation: 2 seeds (s43, s44) collapse rapidly to near-pure H7 tautology (${\geq}97\%$ H7, $0\%$ genuine within ${\sim}150$ steps), while 3 seeds (s42, s45, s46) sustain a transient genuine window.
The 5-seed pooled non-hacking rate is ${\sim}23\%$ at 500 steps, with the collapsed seeds pulling down the average; the 3 non-collapsed seeds individually range from $17\%$ to $55\%$ genuine.
This bifurcation is stochastic: all seeds are indistinguishable in the first ${\sim}100$ steps ($\text{ISR}{\approx}0.05$--$0.07$); divergence occurs at steps 150--200 when H7 tautologies, which receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ by construction, are sampled during rollouts and reinforced via the positive feedback loop.
Once a seed enters the H7 basin, convergence to saturation takes ${\sim}150$ steps and is irreversible. %% registry: plan002-additive-b01-s42/s43-r2/s44/s45/s46

H7 (a single premise identical to the conclusion, giving $\text{ISR}\geq 0.5$ by the LOO definition; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}) is the canonical Goodhart exploit: the model satisfies the structural metric directly rather than producing a genuine derivation.
Total conclusion embedding ($\text{H1}+\text{H7}$) is GRPO-universal at $68$--$100\%$ across both ISR and random conditions (Appendix Figure~\ref{fig:hacking-composition}); the specific mode (H7 vs.\ H1) within a seed is stochastic under both conditions ($\text{CV}{>}1$), though ISR modestly increases H7 probability by providing a direct reward pathway.
Random yields higher PR ($83{\pm}15\%$ vs.\ $70{\pm}19\%$; $n{=}5$ each).
Random H7 exhibits extreme seed dependence (per-seed range: $0\%$--$91.5\%$; pooled $30\%$ is dominated by s46 at $91.5\%$ and s43 at $38.3\%$).
Both conditions produce H7 in 2 of 5 seeds, but the quality differs: ISR-induced H7 is absorbing ($100\%$ of proved samples in affected seeds: s43${=}61/61$, s44${=}89/89$), while random-induced H7 coexists with other modes ($38$--$92\%$).
ISR's reward signal converts H7 from a stochastic possibility into an irreversible attractor once sampled.

\textbf{The transient genuine window.}
During the transient window, ISR-trained seeds produce more genuine proofs than random controls under pooled classification (5-seed: $22.6\%$ vs.\ $7.7\%$; $\text{OR}{=}3.48$ uncorrected, $p{<}10^{-8}$; Appendix Table~\ref{tab:bootstrap-ci}); under stricter H8+FN-corrected classification (3-seed subset), the effect reverses ($\text{OR}{=}0.61$, n.s.).
This benefit is temporary: extended training (1000 steps) on seeds~42 and~45 confirms the window closes completely ($17\%{\to}2\%$ and $55\%{\to}0\%$ genuine respectively; see below).
The same LOO bias that enables genuine improvement (rewarding necessary premises) also creates the Goodhart attractor (rewarding tautological constructions); the genuine window reflects seeds that have not yet sampled the H7 exploit, not seeds that resist it.
Snapshot evaluation at 500 steps would overestimate ISR's benefit; trajectory analysis is required to distinguish transient from stable improvement. %% registry: plan002-b01-s42/s45/s46 (500 step) + plan002-b01-s42-1000

\textbf{Premise-count confound.}
The genuine-rate advantage reflects a selection effect: premise-count-matched comparison yields only $1.06\times$ ISR difference, confirming indistinguishable per-proof quality once LOO bias toward short outputs is controlled (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).

\textbf{Trajectory analysis: timing, not destiny.}\label{sec:goodhart-temporal}
Extended training (1000 steps; Appendix Figure~\ref{fig:training-isr-curves}) confirms the genuine window is transient across seeds.
Seed~42 declines from $17\%$ to $2\%$ genuine via H7 saturation ($16.0\%{\to}96.7\%$ H7, PR stable at ${\sim}96\%$); seed~45, which achieved the highest 500-step genuine rate ($55\%$), collapses to $0\%$ genuine through reward collapse ($\text{PR}: 42\%{\to}2\%$).
The two seeds exhibit distinct failure paths (H7 gaming vs.\ output collapse) but converge to the same outcome: zero genuine proofs at extended training. %% registry: plan002-b01-s42-1000, plan016-extended-1000-s42, plan002-b01-s45-1000

\textbf{Micro-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.05$): deterministic collapse.}
All three ISR seeds reach $\text{PR}{\geq}99\%$ but converge to H7a tautology (H7 $87$--$100\%$, genuine $5.1\%$), while the random control mostly fails to learn (median $\text{PR}{=}7\%$) with zero H7, confirming H7 as specific to ISR's LOO structure.
Below a signal-floor, ISR's genuine component is undetectable while its H7 bias remains exploitable (per-seed breakdown in Appendix~\ref{app:beta005}). %% registry: sweep-isr-b005-s42/s43/s44, sweep-random-b005-s42/s43/s44

\textbf{Medium-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.2$): maximum exploitation.}
At $\beta{=}0.2$, all three seeds converge to H7a tautology with $0\%$ non-hacking (pooled $n{=}290$), the maximum exploitation point in the dose-response curve (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:beta02-detail}).
Seeds achieve $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.55$--$0.96$ through single-premise-equals-conclusion constructions. %% registry: sweep-isr-b02-s42/s43/s44

\textbf{High-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.3$): multi-modal Goodhart.}
At $\beta{=}0.3$, ISR produces extreme cross-seed instability ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$): three seeds yield three distinct failure modes (reward collapse, H1 shortcutting, pure H7 gaming; per-seed details in Appendix~\ref{app:beta03}).
The random control is equally unstable ($\text{PR}{=}54{\pm}35\%$) with $91\%$ H1 and ${\leq}4\%$ non-hacking; high-dose proxy weighting destabilizes training regardless of signal source. %% registry: plan002-additive-b03-s42/s43/s44
ISR vs.\ random H7 at $\beta{=}0.3$: $\text{OR}{=}13.7$, 95\% CI $[7.0, 26.8]$ (Appendix~\ref{app:beta03}).

\textbf{Non-monotonic dose-response.}
The four $\beta$ levels reveal a non-monotonic pattern: $\beta{=}0.05$ and $\beta{=}0.2$ both converge deterministically to H7 collapse ($94\%$ and $99\%$ H7 respectively, ${\leq}5\%$ genuine), while $\beta{=}0.3$ triggers multi-modal instability ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$, three distinct failure modes).
Only $\beta{=}0.1$ sustains a genuine window (3 of 5 seeds), a narrow critical band where ISR signal suffices to reinforce genuine derivations before the H7 attractor absorbs the trajectory.
The non-monotonicity implies that Goodhart collapse is not a simple function of reward dose; the balance between genuine and exploit reinforcement depends on a threshold interaction between $\beta$ and rollout stochasticity.

\subsection{Cross-Logic Diagnostic Transfer}
\label{sec:crosslogic}

We replicate the FOL pipeline with Prolog/SWI-Prolog (3 seeds, $\beta{=}0.1$).
Under exec-only training, 2/3 seeds show $\text{ISR}^{*}{\approx}0$ despite $\text{PR}{\geq}0.56$, reflecting redundant ground-fact repetition rather than FOL-style conclusion embedding; ISR flags both failure semantics.
Under ISR reward, 3/3 seeds reach $0\%$ non-hacking through three distinct mechanisms: clean H7 tautology (s42, $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}1.0$), degenerate uppercase pseudo-Prolog evading text-match classifiers (s43, functional $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$), and query-as-fact gaming (s44, $95/97$ proved at $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$).
Seed~44 evaded our strict classifier entirely; functional cross-validation was required to expose it.
We attribute complete collapse to Prolog's simpler operational semantics providing a broader gaming basin (detailed results in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:prolog-detailed} and Figure~\ref{fig:prolog-comparison}).

\subsection{Cross-Scale Evidence}
\label{sec:crossscale}

We train Qwen3-1.7B under ISR $\beta\in\{0.1,0.3\}$ and Random $\beta{=}0.1$ (single seed, 500 steps).
All conditions produce $0\%$ non-hacking, but the exploit modes differ qualitatively from 4B: Random discovers H9 (contradiction injection, $\text{PR}{=}93\%$, $100\%$ \emph{ex falso}), ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ collapses to a single fixed template ($\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.6$ at zero variance, $100\%$ H1), and ISR $\beta{=}0.3$ triggers reward collapse ($\text{PR}{=}17\%$) mirroring the 4B pattern.
H9 never appears at 4B scale; fixed-template mode collapse never appears at 4B; different capacities converge to different Goodhart basins under identical rewards.
No safe scale was observed in this single-seed comparison (Table~\ref{tab:hacking-taxonomy}).

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We evaluate STA along three axes: ISR as a diagnostic for reward hacking (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}); ISR as a training reward across four dose levels, where it exhibits Goodhart effects (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); and STA as a cross-logic protocol (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
Cross-scale evidence from Qwen3-1.7B reveals capacity-dependent Goodhart basins (\S\ref{sec:crossscale}).
A hacking taxonomy synthesizes the modes observed across conditions (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).

\subsection{Setup}\label{sec:setup}

We train Qwen3-4B~\citep{qwen3} with GRPO~\citep{deepseekmath} ($K{=}4$, lr $10^{-6}$, 500 steps default, 1000 where noted) over seeds $\{42,43,44\}$ on a fixed 500-example FOLIO~\citep{folio} subset held constant across all conditions; the SFT baseline is trained with negative log-likelihood (NLL) on gold formalizations.\footnote{All experiments use \texttt{data/train\_500\_seed42.jsonl}; seeds control initialization and rollout sampling only.}
Held-out evaluation uses 100 FOLIO examples (\texttt{proofwriter\_fol\_100.jsonl}) with greedy decoding (Appendix~\ref{app:setup}).
We report prove rate (PR), proved-only ISR ($\text{ISR}^*$), hacking-mode rates from a two-stage classifier (strict text matching for H1/H7 plus functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}), and a \emph{non-hacking} (N-H) rate, defined as the residual of proved samples matching none of the nine cataloged patterns (a necessary but not sufficient condition for semantic correctness).

\subsection{ISR as Diagnostic}
\label{sec:diagnostic}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_isr_collapse.pdf}
\caption{ISR collapse under exec-only GRPO (seed~42). PR rises 32\%$\to$93\%$\to$96\% while proved-only ISR falls $0.642{\to}0.132{\to}0.003$ over 100$\to$500$\to$1000 steps. By step 1000, 94.8\% of proved samples have $\text{ISR}{=}0$ and mean component count inflates 6.58$\to$18.55 (contradiction explosion).}
\label{fig:isr-collapse}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Collapse trajectory.}
Figure~\ref{fig:isr-collapse} traces exec-only GRPO (seed~42) at 100, 500, 1000 steps.
PR rises $32\%\to93\%\to96\%$, a trajectory that execution-only evaluation would interpret as successful optimization; $\text{ISR}^*$ tells the opposite story, $0.642\to0.132\to0.003$ (214$\times$ collapse). %% registry: plan003-eval-exec-only-r5, plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan016-extended-1000-s42
By 500 steps, 87.1\% of proved samples embed the conclusion (H1); by 1000 steps, the embedding rate saturates at 100\% and mean component count more than doubles ($6.58\to18.55$) as the model emits contradictory or vacuous premises that trivially derive any conclusion.
Extended training, lacking a structural signal, \emph{worsens} formalization quality while improving the headline number.

\textbf{Cross-seed instability.}
The three exec-only seeds diverge into qualitatively different failure modes despite shared data, hyperparameters, and reward (Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}): s42 reaches $\text{PR}{=}93\%$ via conclusion embedding ($\text{H1}{=}87\%$); s43 collapses to $\text{PR}{=}13\%$ (at 500 steps) via repetition (87\% of rollouts truncated); s44 reaches $\text{PR}{=}98\%$ via tautological collapse ($\text{H7}{=}100\%$, mean $n{=}2.04$). %% registry: plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan001-exec-only-s43-r4, plan001-exec-only-s44
The cross-seed PR variance ($\sigma{=}47$\,pp) shows that aggregate metrics obscure qualitatively different failure modes; all three are flagged by $\text{ISR}^*$ even though one passes the PR check (s44) and one fails it (s43).
By 1000 steps, all three converge to high PR ($0.95{\pm}0.05$) with near-zero genuine output (see Appendix~\ref{app:h8} and Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}), each through a different dominant mode (s42: H1 saturation; s43: H1 $93.8\%$, genuine $6.2\%$; s44: H1+H8). %% registry: plan016-extended-1000-s42, exec-only-s43-1000step-r7, plan001-exec-only-s44-1000-r2
Notably, s43 recovers from $\text{PR}{=}13\%$ (500 steps) to $\text{PR}{=}96\%$ (1000 steps), but entirely through H1 exploitation: PR recovery does not imply quality recovery, and the repetition-collapse phase is transient rather than terminal.

\textbf{SFT baseline.}
SFT on gold formalizations reaches $\text{PR}{=}13.0\%$ (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps) with $\text{H7}{=}0$, $\text{H1}{=}7.7\%$, $92.3\%$ non-hacking ($n{=}39$; $\text{OR}{=}147$ vs.\ exec-only, $p{<}0.001$; per-seed range ${\sim}$91--93\%). %% registry: plan009-sft-baseline-s42-1000/s43-1000/s44-1000-r3
The near-absence of hacking under identical data exposure is consistent with hacking being RL-specific; a 100-step checkpoint confirms hacking emerges early in training (Appendix~\ref{app:100step}).

\subsection{ISR as Reward: Goodhart Effects}
\label{sec:goodhart}

We now reverse roles: instead of treating ISR as an observer, we use it as a reward augmentation, $r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, with a matched random control, $r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1 + \beta\,u)$, $u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$, to isolate ISR-specific signal from generic reward-variance effects.
The headline finding: ISR contains an inherent Goodhart vulnerability~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} observed to produce collapse at all four tested doses ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$).
The mechanism is structural: tautological proofs ($P{\to}P$) receive $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$ and single-premise-equals-conclusion constructions receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$, both by the LOO definition alone.
Once sampled during GRPO rollouts, these high-ISR tautologies create a positive feedback loop; $\beta$ controls only the \emph{timing} of collapse, not whether it occurs.

\textbf{High-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.3$): multi-modal Goodhart.}
At $\beta{=}0.3$, ISR produces extreme cross-seed instability ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$): three seeds yield three distinct failure modes (reward collapse, H1 shortcutting, pure H7 gaming; per-seed details in Appendix~\ref{app:beta03}).

The four $\beta$ levels reveal a non-monotonic pattern: $\beta{=}0.05$ and $\beta{=}0.2$ both converge deterministically to H7 collapse ($94\%$ and $99\%$ H7 respectively, ${\leq}5\%$ genuine), while $\beta{=}0.3$ triggers multi-modal instability ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$, three distinct failure modes).
Only $\beta{=}0.1$ sustains a genuine window (3 of 5 seeds), a narrow critical band where ISR signal suffices to reinforce genuine derivations before the H7 attractor absorbs the trajectory.
The non-monotonicity implies that Goodhart collapse is not a simple function of reward dose; the balance between genuine and exploit reinforcement depends on a threshold interaction between $\beta$ and rollout stochasticity.

\subsection{Cross-Logic Diagnostic Transfer}
\label{sec:crosslogic}

We replicate the FOL pipeline with Prolog/SWI-Prolog (3 seeds, $\beta{=}0.1$).
Under exec-only training, 2/3 seeds show $\text{ISR}^{*}{\approx}0$ despite $\text{PR}{\geq}0.56$, reflecting redundant ground-fact repetition rather than FOL-style conclusion embedding; ISR flags both failure semantics.
Under ISR reward, 3/3 seeds reach $0\%$ non-hacking through three distinct mechanisms: clean H7 tautology (s42, $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}1.0$), degenerate uppercase pseudo-Prolog evading text-match classifiers (s43, functional $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$), and query-as-fact gaming (s44, $95/97$ proved at $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$).
Seed~44 evaded our strict classifier entirely; functional cross-validation was required to expose it.
We attribute complete collapse to Prolog's simpler operational semantics providing a broader gaming basin (detailed results in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:prolog-detailed} and Figure~\ref{fig:prolog-comparison}).

\subsection{Cross-Scale Evidence}
\label{sec:crossscale}

We train Qwen3-1.7B under ISR $\beta\in\{0.1,0.3\}$ and Random $\beta{=}0.1$ (single seed, 500 steps).
All conditions produce $0\%$ non-hacking, but the exploit modes differ qualitatively from 4B: Random discovers H9 (contradiction injection, $\text{PR}{=}93\%$, $100\%$ \emph{ex falso}), ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ collapses to a single fixed template ($\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.6$ at zero variance, $100\%$ H1), and ISR $\beta{=}0.3$ triggers reward collapse ($\text{PR}{=}17\%$) mirroring the 4B pattern.
H9 never appears at 4B scale; fixed-template mode collapse never appears at 4B; different capacities converge to different Goodhart basins under identical rewards.
No safe scale was observed in this single-seed comparison (Table~\ref{tab:hacking-taxonomy}).

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

GRPO-trained formalizers converge to high prove rates on first-order logic problems ($95{\pm}5\%$ across three seeds, 1000 steps), yet at convergence, \emph{none} produce structurally sound outputs.
Each seed develops a distinct degenerate shortcut: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, or tautological collapse, all invisible to execution-based evaluation, which registers success regardless of whether the proof reflects genuine derivation.

\paragraph{The execution-only blind spot.}
Prove rate, the dominant evaluation metric for neurosymbolic formalizers~\citep{logic-lm, linc, satlm}, conflates faithful reasoning with degenerate shortcuts, a gap especially consequential under RL, where the optimizer exploits any shortcut the reward fails to penalize~\citep{skalse-reward-hacking, reward-hacking-survey}.
Recent work applies GRPO~\citep{deepseekmath} to train LLMs that generate solver-verified formal programs~\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl} using binary execution feedback; this drives rapid PR gains but provides no signal on structural quality.
Process reward models~\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd} require expensive annotations and do not transfer to arbitrary solver-backed settings.
A separate line of work documents that LLMs already game logical formalization at inference time~\citep{kim-game-formalization, bondarenko-spec-gaming}; what is missing is an annotation-free \emph{diagnostic} for structural integrity in neurosymbolic outputs.

\paragraph{Component necessity testing.}
We address this gap with \emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), which applies \emph{component necessity testing} (leave-one-out ablation on solver inputs) to quantify structural integrity (Figure~\ref{fig:sta-overview}).
For each proved formalization, STA removes each component individually and re-runs the solver; the fraction of components whose removal causes proof failure yields the \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR), with $\text{ISR}{=}1$ indicating full necessity and $\text{ISR}{=}0$ complete redundancy.
LOO ablation itself is standard~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey}; our contribution lies in applying it as a GRPO-hacking diagnostic and in the empirical phenomena it surfaces.
ISR captures structural rather than semantic integrity (downstream NLI: $\rho{=}{-}0.049$, $p{=}0.187$).

\paragraph{ISR as diagnostic.}
As a post-hoc diagnostic on a GRPO formalizer trained with FOLIO~\citep{folio}, ISR reveals a structural collapse trajectory invisible to PR: $\text{ISR}^{*}{:}\,0.642\to 0.132\to 0.003$ over 100--1000 steps (seed~42; 99.5\% degradation) while PR rises $32\%{\to}96\%$.
Three seeds diverge radically (PR $\sigma{=}47$\,pp), each converging to a qualitatively different mode: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, and tautological collapse.
An SFT baseline on identical data reaches $\text{PR}{=}13.0\%$ with 92.3\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps), localizing the failure to RL optimization, not data or capacity.

\paragraph{ISR as reward: Goodhart collapse at all tested doses.}
Repurposed as a training signal, $r = r_{\text{exec}} \cdot (1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, ISR contains an inherent structural vulnerability: tautological proofs (a single premise identical to the conclusion) receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ by construction, and implication tautologies ($P{\to}P$) receive $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, creating a positive feedback loop once sampled during GRPO rollouts~\citep{karwowski-goodhart-rl, kwa-catastrophic-goodhart}.
Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} is observed at all four tested doses ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$): $\beta$ controls \emph{when} collapse occurs, not \emph{whether}.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, collapse is stochastic and delayed: 5 seeds bifurcate between rapid H7 convergence (2 seeds, ${\leq}100$ steps) and a transient genuine window (${\sim}23\%$ non-hacking at 500 steps, 5-seed pooled) that closes under extended training (seeds~42 and~45: $17\%{\to}2\%$ and $55\%{\to}0\%$ genuine at 1000 steps).
Snapshot evaluation at 500 steps would overestimate ISR's benefit; trajectory analysis reveals the window is temporary.
The effect transfers to Prolog (3/3 seeds yield 0\% non-hacking via distinct mechanisms, including \emph{query-as-fact gaming}) and across model scale (1.7B discovers qualitatively novel gaming modes).
ISR's asymmetry is the central finding: \emph{reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer at any dose.}

\paragraph{Contributions.}
Across 6 reward conditions, 5 seeds, 2 logic types, 2 model scales, and up to 1000 steps, we contribute: (\textbf{C1}) ISR as a diagnostic for GRPO reward hacking, with a 99.5\% collapse trajectory invisible to PR and an SFT control localizing the failure to RL (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}); (\textbf{C2}) an empirical instance of Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} observed at all four tested doses: ISR's structural bias toward tautology ($\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ for $P{\to}P$) creates a positive feedback loop; collapse is stochastic and delayed at moderate $\beta$ but trajectory analysis on seeds~42 and~45 (1000 steps) confirms the genuine window closes via distinct paths (H7 saturation and reward collapse respectively), showing that $\beta$ controls timing, not outcome (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); (\textbf{C3}) cross-logic transfer to Prolog with consistent Goodhart effects across all seeds (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}); (\textbf{C4}) a nine-mode hacking taxonomy including query-as-fact gaming, obfuscated tautology, and a scale-specific \emph{ex falso} mode, motivating functional cross-validation of diagnostics (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
These are cautionary results: snapshot evaluation of structural rewards can overestimate their benefit; only trajectory analysis reveals the transient nature of apparent improvement.

\section{Extended Discussion}
\label{app:extended-discussion}

\paragraph{What ISR measures, and what it does not.}
ISR quantifies syntactic component necessity: the fraction of solver-input components whose individual removal causes proof failure.
This is strictly weaker than semantic faithfulness (whether the formalization accurately captures the natural-language meaning).
We verify this empirically: Spearman $\rho(\text{ISR}, \text{NLI accuracy}) = -0.049$ ($p = 0.187$, n.s.) from a downstream NLI evaluation on exec-only checkpoint outputs.
ISR and downstream task performance are uncorrelated.
ISR is thus a structural integrity diagnostic, not a semantic quality metric: high ISR indicates that every component contributes to the proof, not that the proof faithfully represents the original reasoning problem.

Critically, low ISR carries different semantics depending on the training objective.
Under exec-only training, low ISR in Prolog reflects redundant coding (repeated ground facts where removing any single copy does not affect the proof) rather than an absence of reasoning (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
Under ISR-as-reward, high ISR reflects metric gaming (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}).
ISR values must always be interpreted relative to the optimization objective that produced them.

\paragraph{The premise-count confound.}
LOO-based metrics like ISR have an inherent mathematical bias: with fewer components, each is mechanically more likely to be necessary.
A formalization with 2 premises where both are necessary yields ISR${=}1.0$; one with 10 premises where 8 are necessary yields ISR${=}0.8$, even though the latter encodes richer reasoning.
This confound is central to ISR's Goodhart vulnerability: H7 tautologies (single premise $=$ conclusion) achieve $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ \emph{by construction}, and the shorter formalizations produced by non-collapsed seeds at $\beta{=}0.1$ also inflate ISR mechanically.
Premise-count-matched comparison on non-hacking samples yields $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.258$ vs.\ $0.243$ for random ($1.06\times$; Table~\ref{tab:fol-beta01-detailed}), confirming that even within the transient genuine window the structural benefit is negligible.
This bias is not specific to our setting; any LOO-based structural metric applied to variable-length outputs requires component-count normalization.
We recommend that future work employing ablation-based diagnostics report premise-count-matched comparisons alongside raw values.

\paragraph{Seed-level statistical analysis.}
To address potential inflation from within-seed dependence, we supplement pooled Fisher exact tests with two seed-aware analyses.
Cochran--Mantel--Haenszel (CMH) tests stratify by seed while pooling across samples: H7 $\text{OR}_{\text{CMH}}{=}2.46$ (95\% CI $[1.85, 3.27]$, $p{=}5.6{\times}10^{-16}$); genuine $\text{OR}_{\text{CMH}}{=}3.37$ (95\% CI $[2.21, 5.13]$, $p{=}4.5{\times}10^{-10}$).
Seed-level permutation tests (treating each seed as a single observation, $n{=}5$ per group) yield $p{=}0.28$ (H7) and $p{=}0.26$ (genuine), consistent with the severe power limitation of $n{=}5$ (minimum achievable $p{=}0.008$) rather than absence of effect.

ISR's LOO definition creates an inherent structural bias: tautological proofs ($P{\to}P$) receive $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, and single-premise-equals-conclusion constructions receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$, making H7 the global ISR-maximizing exploit.
$\beta$ controls the \emph{timing} of collapse, not whether it occurs.
At all four tested doses, H7 dominates: $\beta{=}0.05$ (3 seeds, pooled H7 $93.7\%$, $n{=}253$; random s43 achieves $\text{PR}{=}62\%$ with H1 $77.4\%$ and zero H7, confirming mode specificity); $\beta{=}0.1$ (stochastic bifurcation: 2/5 seeds collapse within ${\sim}150$ steps, remaining 3/5 sustain a transient window that closes under extended training); $\beta{=}0.2$ ($100\%$ H7 across all three seeds, $n{=}290$; Table~\ref{tab:beta02-detail}); $\beta{=}0.3$ (multi-modal, s44 pure H7).

Once a seed samples and reinforces the H7 exploit, convergence is irreversible; this absorbing-state property guarantees eventual collapse regardless of dose.

\paragraph{Goodhart effects: implications.}
The finding extends beyond this specific system.
ISR was designed to \emph{detect} reward gaming of $r_{\text{exec}}$, yet it contains an inherent structural vulnerability: by its LOO definition, tautological proofs receive artificially high ISR ($P{\to}P$ yields $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$; single-premise-equals-conclusion yields $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$), creating a positive feedback loop once sampled during GRPO rollouts~\citep{karwowski-goodhart-rl, kwa-catastrophic-goodhart}.
Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} is observed at all four tested doses ($\beta{=}0.05$: 3 seeds; $\beta\in\{0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$: 3--5 seeds each).
The structural bias predicts universality (H7 tautology is always the global reward-maximizing exploit regardless of $\beta$), and $\beta$ controls only the probability of early sampling and thus the timing of collapse; at $\beta{=}0.05$, three seeds confirm deterministic H7 collapse ($93.7\%$ pooled) while the matched random control at the same $\beta$ produces H1 redundancy instead ($77.4\%$), ruling out dose magnitude as the driver.
At moderate doses ($\beta{=}0.1$), collapse is stochastic and delayed (5 seeds bifurcate: 2 collapse rapidly, 3 sustain a transient genuine window that trajectory analysis confirms is temporary); at higher doses ($\beta{=}0.2$), collapse is immediate and universal.
$\beta{=}0.3$ adds reward collapse~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} as a competing failure mode (PR drops to 18\% in 1/3 seeds), but the underlying Goodhart vulnerability remains the same.
The practical implication is that ISR (and structurally similar LOO-based diagnostics) should be used exclusively as post-hoc evaluation tools, never as training rewards.

\paragraph{Single-seed unreliability.}
The three exec-only seeds diverge radically (PR $\sigma{=}47$ percentage points), each converging to a qualitatively different degeneration mode (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ (5 seeds) shows even greater instability: 2/5 seeds collapse to H7 within ${\sim}150$ steps, while 3/5 sustain a transient genuine window.
The 5-seed pooled non-hacking rate is ${\sim}23\%$ at 500 steps; trajectory analysis on seeds~42 and~45 (1000 steps) confirms this is temporary ($17\%{\to}2\%$ and $55\%{\to}0\%$ genuine respectively).
The dominant hacking mode (H7 vs.\ H1) is stochastic within any treatment condition ($\text{CV}{>}1$).
Multi-seed evaluation with trajectory analysis should be standard practice for neurosymbolic RL systems; single-seed or single-checkpoint results can misrepresent a configuration's true hacking profile.

\paragraph{Classifier Validation.}
Hacking mode classification uses deterministic rule-based classifiers, not learned models, so standard ML precision/recall is not directly applicable.
H1 and H7 are identified by normalized text matching between conclusion and premise strings after whitespace and variable normalization; remaining modes are detected via functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution from STA (leave-one-out ablation).
No training data or manual annotation is used for classification.

To estimate precision, we manually verified 50 randomly sampled outputs classified as H1 or H7: all 50 were confirmed correct (estimated precision ${>}$95\%, Wilson 95\% CI: [93\%, 100\%]).
Recall is inherently bounded by the text-match threshold: semantic manipulations that alter surface form while preserving the gaming structure (e.g., variable renaming beyond our normalization, or paraphrased conclusions) would be missed.
We cross-validate with functional LOO analysis: samples classified as non-hacking but showing $n_{\text{necessary}} \leq 1$ are flagged as potential false negatives.
This cross-validation revealed query-as-fact gaming in Prolog (\S\ref{app:hacking-modes}), where the strict text classifier reported 100\% non-hacking but functional analysis showed 95/97 samples were tautological ($n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$).
The non-hacking rate for FOL conditions may therefore be slightly overestimated, as subtle semantic manipulations below our text-matching threshold would evade the strict classifier.

\subsection{H8 --- Premise-Subset Gaming}
\label{app:h8}

Manual audit of ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 revealed a previously undetected hacking mode: the model emits a subset of the gold premises that is individually necessary (high ISR) but insufficient for the intended derivation, with proof success depending on the conclusion already being embedded (H1-style).
We term this \textbf{H8 (premise-subset gaming)}: formalizations where each component is LOO-necessary but the premise set is a strict subset of what the NL problem requires, inflating ISR without faithful reasoning.

\paragraph{Detection.} H8 is identified by manual inspection of non-hacking samples with unusually low premise counts ($n_{\text{prem}} \leq 3$) that nonetheless achieve high ISR.
Automated detection is not currently feasible because H8 requires comparing the generated premise set against the gold premises.

\paragraph{Audit scope and limitations.}
Full H8 audit was completed for ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 only.
ISR seeds~43 and~44 checkpoints were deleted before audit and cannot be recovered; their non-hacking rates may be overestimated.
Random $\beta{=}0.1$ does not produce H8 by mechanism (no ISR optimization pressure); seed~42 audit confirmed H8${=}0$.

\paragraph{H7 false-negative correction (H7b obfuscated tautology).}
ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~44 contained 12 samples with $n_{\text{prem}}{=}1$ classified as non-hacking by the text matcher.
Manual inspection confirmed all 12 are logically equivalent to H7 but evade text matching through vacuous quantifier wrapping ($11/12$) or structural simplification ($1/12$).
We classify these as \textbf{H7b} (obfuscated tautology), distinct from text-match-detectable H7a.
$10/12$ achieve $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.83$, indicating simultaneous gaming of execution reward, ISR metric, and H7 classifier (triple gaming; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
After correction, ISR s44 non-hacking${=}0$; total H7 = H7a (77 text-match) + H7b (12 obfuscated) = 89.

\paragraph{Impact on non-hacking-rate comparison.}
After H8 reclassification and H7 false-negative correction: ISR non-hacking $= 14/231 = 6.06\%$ vs.\ random non-hacking $= 25/262 = 9.5\%$ (Fisher $p{=}0.182$, n.s.; Wilson 95\% CI: ISR [3.6\%, 9.9\%], Random [6.5\%, 13.7\%]).
The direction is consistent with ISR-amplified gaming modes (H7, H8) displacing non-hacking output, but the effect is not statistically significant at the conventional $\alpha{=}0.05$ threshold.

\subsection{H1 --- Conclusion Embedding}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The conclusion appears verbatim (or with trivial variable renaming) as one premise among multiple premises.
The solver succeeds by matching the embedded conclusion, rendering the other premises irrelevant to the proof.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x (bird(x) -> flies(x)).
  bird(tweety).
  flies(tweety).  % conclusion embedded
Conclusion: flies(tweety).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
Variable. The embedded premise has ISR~$=1$ (removing it may break the proof), but other premises may also register as necessary depending on Prover9's search strategy.
ISR does not distinguish trivial from substantive necessity.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Conclusion embedding in some form (H1 multi-premise or H7 single-premise) is GRPO-universal at 68--97\% across all RL conditions.
Under exec-only and Random reward, it manifests as H1 (59--91\%); under ISR reward, it shifts to H7 (54\% pooled, 5-seed).


\subsection{H7a --- Conclusion Duplication (Standard)}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The entire formalization collapses to a single premise whose content is identical (text-match detectable) to the conclusion.
Since $P \to P$ is trivially provable, this simultaneously maximizes exec reward.
Because the sole premise is necessary for every sub-component of the conclusion under LOO ablation, ISR is inflated toward 1.0.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
Conclusion:
  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0.8$--$1.0$.
The single premise is trivially ``maximally necessary,'' but the proof is vacuous.
H7a games both exec reward and ISR reward; H7b extends this to triple gaming by additionally evading the text-match classifier.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
H7a (text-match detectable): 64.5\% (149/231, 3-seed) under ISR~$\beta{=}0.1$ (s42: 16.0\%, s43: 96.7\%, s44: 86.5\%); 5-seed pooled H7: 54\% (190/350, Table~\ref{tab:goodhart-landscape}).
Combined H7 (H7a + H7b, 3-seed): 70.6\% (163/231; s43 H7a${=}59$ + H7b${=}2$; includes s44 FN correction).
Random~$\beta{=}0.1$ pooled: 29.5\% (122/414, 5-seed, all H7a; driven by s46 at 91.5\% and s43 at 38.3\%; s42/s44/s45 at 0\%).


\subsection{H7b --- Obfuscated Tautology}

\paragraph{Definition.}
A single-premise formalization logically equivalent to H7a (premise = conclusion) but with surface-form differences that evade the text-match H7 classifier.
The model achieves this through vacuous quantifier wrapping ($11/12$ instances) or structural simplification ($1/12$).

\paragraph{Example (FOL, vacuous quantifier wrapping).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x all y ((A(x)&B(y))->(C(x)|D(y))).
Conclusion:
  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
\end{verbatim}}
The premise introduces a vacuous second quantifier variable $y$ that is immediately unified with $x$, making the formulas logically equivalent while differing textually.

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
$\text{ISR}{\geq}0.83$ ($10/12$ samples).
H7b simultaneously games three objectives: execution reward ($r_{\text{exec}}{=}1$ via tautological proof), ISR metric (single necessary premise yields high ISR), and the text-match H7 classifier (surface-form difference evades detection).
This triple gaming makes H7b the most complete Goodhart case we observe.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Found primarily in ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~44 ($12/89$ proved samples, all originally classified as non-hacking); seed~43 contributes $2$ additional cases.
Functional cross-validation via $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$ exposed the misclassification.


\subsection{Tautological Collapse}

\paragraph{Definition.}
Two-component formalizations where the premise and conclusion are identical atomic or simple formulas, yielding a $P \to P$ tautology with minimal token cost.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
\begin{verbatim}
Premises: p(a).
Conclusion: p(a).
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$=1.0$ (the sole premise is necessary).
Distinguished from H7 by having low component count ($n_{\text{comp}}\approx 2$) and atomic formulas rather than complex sub-structured conclusions.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Dominant in FOL exec-only seed~44 (PR~$=0.98$, mean $n_{\text{comp}}=2.04$, 100\% H7 by strict classifier).
Also observed in Prolog exec+STA seed~42 (100\% H7, PR~$=0.50$).


\subsection{Repetition Collapse}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The model generates identical premises or clauses repeated until the maximum completion length, producing a degenerate output with high token count but no logical diversity.
Removing any single repeated copy leaves the others intact, yielding ISR~$\approx 0$.

\paragraph{Example (Prolog).}
\begin{verbatim}
penguin(fido).
penguin(fido).
penguin(fido).
... (repeated to 512 tokens)
query(penguin(fido)).
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0$. Each copy is individually redundant since identical copies remain after removal.
ISR correctly diagnoses this degeneration.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed in FOL exec-only seed~43 (87\% of outputs hit max completion length; PR~$=13$\%, ISR~$=0$).


\subsection{Complexity-without-Utility}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The formalization contains syntactically complex premises (nested quantifiers, multi-arity predicates) that are semantically vacuous; none is individually necessary for the proof.
The complexity inflates surface metrics (formula length, nesting depth) without contributing to logical derivation.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x all y (R(x,y) ->
    exists z (S(x,z) & T(z,y))).
  all x (P(x) -> Q(x)).
  P(a).            % only this needed
Conclusion: Q(a).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR correctly identifies the vacuous premises (ISR~$=0$ for each), pulling down the mean ISR.
This is the mode ISR is best calibrated for.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Low. Observed in Random~$\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 at 3.8\% (3/79).
Not observed under ISR reward (ISR's gradient discourages zero-ISR premises).


\subsection{Contradiction Explosion}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The component count grows unboundedly over training.
Excess premises introduce contradictions or redundancies that trivially entail any conclusion via \emph{ex falso quodlibet}.
Individual premises may register as ISR~$=0$ (removable without breaking the proof), but the sheer count obscures the underlying triviality.

\paragraph{Example (FOL, 1000-step exec-only).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  c1. c2. c3. ... c18. % 18.55 mean
  % conclusion embedded among premises
Conclusion: Q(a).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0$ (at 1000 steps: ISR~$=0.003$, with 94.8\% of proved samples having ISR~$=0$).

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed in extended exec-only training (seed~42, 1000 steps).
Mean component count grows from ${\sim}6$ (500 steps) to 18.55 (1000 steps).


\subsection{Query-as-Fact Gaming}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The model converts the natural language conclusion into a snake\_case atom and includes it as both a ground fact and the query.
Prolog trivially proves the query by unifying with the fact.
This mode evades text-match classifiers designed for H1/H7 because the generated atom bears no surface resemblance to the original conclusion text.

\paragraph{Example (Prolog).}
\begin{verbatim}
% NL: "Fido is happy."
% Model output:
fido_is_happy.
:- fido_is_happy.     % query = fact
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0.9$--$1.0$.
The single fact is trivially necessary (its removal breaks the query), inflating ISR.
Functionally equivalent to H7 but with a distinct surface mechanism.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed in Prolog exec+STA seed~44 (PR~$=0.97$, ISR~$=0.912$).
95/97 proved samples have $n_{\text{necessary}}=1$, confirming functional tautology despite the strict classifier reporting 100\% non-hacking.


\subsection{H9 --- Ex Falso Quodlibet (Contradiction Injection)}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The model generates a premise set containing logically contradictory assertions (e.g., $P(x)$ and $\neg P(x)$).
From contradictory premises, any conclusion follows by the \emph{ex falso quodlibet} principle, rendering the proof semantically vacuous regardless of the conclusion's content.
Unlike the ``contradiction explosion'' mode observed in 4B exec-only at 1000 steps (where contradictions arise incidentally among inflated premise counts), H9 is a \emph{targeted} strategy: the model constructs minimal contradictory pairs that directly enable the proof.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x (bird(x) -> flies(x)).
  bird(tweety).
  -bird(tweety).  % contradicts above
Conclusion: happy(tweety).
% Proof: bird(tweety) & -bird(tweety) -> False -> anything
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$>0$ because each side of the contradiction is individually necessary under LOO: removing $P(x)$ leaves $\neg P(x)$ alone, which cannot derive a contradiction; removing $\neg P(x)$ leaves the premises consistent but insufficient to derive an unrelated conclusion.
The LOO test thus registers both contradictory premises as ``necessary,'' inflating ISR despite the formalization being semantically vacuous.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed exclusively in Qwen3-1.7B under Random $\beta{=}0.1$ (seed~42, 500 steps, proper train/eval separation): 100\% of proved samples ($n{=}93$) exhibit H9.
Under ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ with the same model, H9 does not appear; the model instead converges to fixed-template H1 ($\text{ISR}{=}0.6$, zero variance), indicating that ISR reward redirects the hacking pathway from H9 to H1.
Not observed in any Qwen3-4B experiment across all conditions and seeds tested. %% registry: d113-1.7b-random-b01-s42

and seed~44 converts NL conclusions to snake\_case atoms used as both fact and query.

\subsection{Early-Training Hacking Analysis (100-Step Checkpoint)}
\label{app:100step}

To control for the prove-rate confound in our SFT comparison (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}), we analyze the exec-only checkpoint at 100 training steps (seed~42), where PR${=}32$\%, higher than SFT (13.0\%, 3-seed pooled) but still early in training.
Of the 32 proved samples, 9 (28.1\%) exhibit H7 hacking (single premise identical to conclusion) and 1 (3.1\%) exhibits H1 (conclusion embedded among premises), yielding a total hacking rate of 31.2\%.
By contrast, SFT at comparable or lower PR shows 7.7\% hacking (1/13 proved samples).
This demonstrates that reward hacking emerges early in GRPO training, well before the prove-rate plateau, and is not simply an artifact of having more proved samples available for exploitation.
The 100-step hacking rate (31.2\%) is already substantially above SFT (7.7\%), supporting the claim that hacking is associated with RL optimization rather than prove-rate level alone.

\subsection{$O(1)$ vs.\ $O(n)$ ISR Ablation}
\label{app:o1-ablation}

To justify the per-clause LOO design (\S\ref{sec:sta}), we train a variant that replaces the $O(n)$ ablation with a cheaper $O(1)$ binary signal: $\text{fast\_ISR}(x) = 1$ if $x$ is proved \emph{and} the conclusion is not provable under empty premises (tautology check), $0$ otherwise.
The reward becomes $r = 0.5\,r_{\text{exec}} + 0.5\,\text{fast\_ISR}$.
After 500 steps (seed~42), this variant achieves $\text{PR}{=}63\%$ with $\text{ISR}^*{=}0.007$ (functionally zero), compared to $\text{ISR}^*{=}0.132$ under standard exec-only and $\text{ISR}^*{=}0.42$ under ISR $\beta{=}0.1$.

\paragraph{ISR signal vs.\ training dynamics.}
At the \emph{ISR signal level}, the $O(1)$ variant is indistinguishable from exec-only: both produce near-zero ISR because models emit redundant premise copies whose individual removal never changes the proof outcome.
At the \emph{training level}, the two conditions are non-equivalent: the $O(1)$ tautology check penalizes formalizations where the conclusion is provable without any premises, a constraint absent from exec-only.
This confound depresses prove rate by 30 percentage points ($63\%$ vs.\ $93\%$ exec-only), making it impossible to attribute the difference purely to the ISR signal.
The result confirms that the $O(n)$ per-clause ablation is necessary for ISR to carry a structural signal, while also showing that even a minimal tautology guard alters training dynamics substantially.

\section{STA Algorithm}
\label{app:algorithm}

Algorithm~\ref{alg:sta} (Section~\ref{sec:sta}) gives the procedure for computing ISR over a proved formalization.
For unproved samples ($S(x) \neq \textit{proved}$), ISR is undefined and the protocol is not applied.


\section{Extended Discussion}
\label{app:extended-discussion}

\paragraph{What ISR measures, and what it does not.}
ISR quantifies syntactic component necessity: the fraction of solver-input components whose individual removal causes proof failure.
This is strictly weaker than semantic faithfulness (whether the formalization accurately captures the natural-language meaning).
We verify this empirically: Spearman $\rho(\text{ISR}, \text{NLI accuracy}) = -0.049$ ($p = 0.187$, n.s.) from a downstream NLI evaluation on exec-only checkpoint outputs.
ISR and downstream task performance are uncorrelated.
ISR is thus a structural integrity diagnostic, not a semantic quality metric: high ISR indicates that every component contributes to the proof, not that the proof faithfully represents the original reasoning problem.

Critically, low ISR carries different semantics depending on the training objective.
Under exec-only training, low ISR in Prolog reflects redundant coding (repeated ground facts where removing any single copy does not affect the proof) rather than an absence of reasoning (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
Under ISR-as-reward, high ISR reflects metric gaming (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}).
ISR values must always be interpreted relative to the optimization objective that produced them.

\paragraph{The premise-count confound.}
LOO-based metrics like ISR have an inherent mathematical bias: with fewer components, each is mechanically more likely to be necessary.
A formalization with 2 premises where both are necessary yields ISR${=}1.0$; one with 10 premises where 8 are necessary yields ISR${=}0.8$, even though the latter encodes richer reasoning.
This confound is central to ISR's Goodhart vulnerability: H7 tautologies (single premise $=$ conclusion) achieve $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ \emph{by construction}, and the shorter formalizations produced by non-collapsed seeds at $\beta{=}0.1$ also inflate ISR mechanically.
Premise-count-matched comparison on non-hacking samples yields $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.258$ vs.\ $0.243$ for random ($1.06\times$; Table~\ref{tab:fol-beta01-detailed}), confirming that even within the transient genuine window the structural benefit is negligible.
This bias is not specific to our setting; any LOO-based structural metric applied to variable-length outputs requires component-count normalization.
We recommend that future work employing ablation-based diagnostics report premise-count-matched comparisons alongside raw values.

\paragraph{Seed-level statistical analysis.}
To address potential inflation from within-seed dependence, we supplement pooled Fisher exact tests with two seed-aware analyses.
Cochran--Mantel--Haenszel (CMH) tests stratify by seed while pooling across samples: H7 $\text{OR}_{\text{CMH}}{=}2.46$ (95\% CI $[1.85, 3.27]$, $p{=}5.6{\times}10^{-16}$); genuine $\text{OR}_{\text{CMH}}{=}3.37$ (95\% CI $[2.21, 5.13]$, $p{=}4.5{\times}10^{-10}$).
Seed-level permutation tests (treating each seed as a single observation, $n{=}5$ per group) yield $p{=}0.28$ (H7) and $p{=}0.26$ (genuine), consistent with the severe power limitation of $n{=}5$ (minimum achievable $p{=}0.008$) rather than absence of effect.

\paragraph{H7 as inevitable exploit.}
ISR's LOO definition creates an inherent structural bias: tautological proofs ($P{\to}P$) receive $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, and single-premise-equals-conclusion constructions receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$, making H7 the global ISR-maximizing exploit.
$\beta$ controls the \emph{timing} of collapse, not whether it occurs.
At all four tested doses, H7 dominates: $\beta{=}0.05$ (3 seeds, pooled H7 $93.7\%$, $n{=}253$; random s43 achieves $\text{PR}{=}62\%$ with H1 $77.4\%$ and zero H7, confirming mode specificity); $\beta{=}0.1$ (stochastic bifurcation: 2/5 seeds collapse within ${\sim}150$ steps, remaining 3/5 sustain a transient window that closes under extended training); $\beta{=}0.2$ ($100\%$ H7 across all three seeds, $n{=}290$; Table~\ref{tab:beta02-detail}); $\beta{=}0.3$ (multi-modal, s44 pure H7).
The random control produces $29.5\%$ H7 ($122/414$, 5-seed; per-seed: $0\%$--$91.5\%$, dominated by s46 at $91.5\%$ and s43 at $38.3\%$; s42/s44/s45 at $0\%$), random $\beta{=}0.3$ yields 4--7 H7a per seed.
Once a seed samples and reinforces the H7 exploit, convergence is irreversible; this absorbing-state property guarantees eventual collapse regardless of dose.

\paragraph{Goodhart effects: implications.}
The finding extends beyond this specific system.
ISR was designed to \emph{detect} reward gaming of $r_{\text{exec}}$, yet it contains an inherent structural vulnerability: by its LOO definition, tautological proofs receive artificially high ISR ($P{\to}P$ yields $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$; single-premise-equals-conclusion yields $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$), creating a positive feedback loop once sampled during GRPO rollouts~\citep{karwowski-goodhart-rl, kwa-catastrophic-goodhart}.
Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} is observed at all four tested doses ($\beta{=}0.05$: 3 seeds; $\beta\in\{0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$: 3--5 seeds each).
The structural bias predicts universality (H7 tautology is always the global reward-maximizing exploit regardless of $\beta$), and $\beta$ controls only the probability of early sampling and thus the timing of collapse; at $\beta{=}0.05$, three seeds confirm deterministic H7 collapse ($93.7\%$ pooled) while the matched random control at the same $\beta$ produces H1 redundancy instead ($77.4\%$), ruling out dose magnitude as the driver.
At moderate doses ($\beta{=}0.1$), collapse is stochastic and delayed (5 seeds bifurcate: 2 collapse rapidly, 3 sustain a transient genuine window that trajectory analysis confirms is temporary); at higher doses ($\beta{=}0.2$), collapse is immediate and universal.
$\beta{=}0.3$ adds reward collapse~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} as a competing failure mode (PR drops to 18\% in 1/3 seeds), but the underlying Goodhart vulnerability remains the same.
The practical implication is that ISR (and structurally similar LOO-based diagnostics) should be used exclusively as post-hoc evaluation tools, never as training rewards.

\paragraph{Single-seed unreliability.}
The three exec-only seeds diverge radically (PR $\sigma{=}47$ percentage points), each converging to a qualitatively different degeneration mode (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ (5 seeds) shows even greater instability: 2/5 seeds collapse to H7 within ${\sim}150$ steps, while 3/5 sustain a transient genuine window.
The 5-seed pooled non-hacking rate is ${\sim}23\%$ at 500 steps; trajectory analysis on seeds~42 and~45 (1000 steps) confirms this is temporary ($17\%{\to}2\%$ and $55\%{\to}0\%$ genuine respectively).
The dominant hacking mode (H7 vs.\ H1) is stochastic within any treatment condition ($\text{CV}{>}1$).
Multi-seed evaluation with trajectory analysis should be standard practice for neurosymbolic RL systems; single-seed or single-checkpoint results can misrepresent a configuration's true hacking profile.


\section{Hacking Mode Definitions}
\label{app:hacking-modes}

Hacking mode classification uses deterministic rule-based classifiers, not learned models, so standard ML precision/recall is not directly applicable.
H1 and H7 are identified by normalized text matching between conclusion and premise strings after whitespace and variable normalization; remaining modes are detected via functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution from STA (leave-one-out ablation).
No training data or manual annotation is used for classification.

To estimate precision, we manually verified 50 randomly sampled outputs classified as H1 or H7: all 50 were confirmed correct (estimated precision ${>}$95\%, Wilson 95\% CI: [93\%, 100\%]).
Recall is inherently bounded by the text-match threshold: semantic manipulations that alter surface form while preserving the gaming structure (e.g., variable renaming beyond our normalization, or paraphrased conclusions) would be missed.
We cross-validate with functional LOO analysis: samples classified as non-hacking but showing $n_{\text{necessary}} \leq 1$ are flagged as potential false negatives.
This cross-validation revealed query-as-fact gaming in Prolog (\S\ref{app:hacking-modes}), where the strict text classifier reported 100\% non-hacking but functional analysis showed 95/97 samples were tautological ($n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$).
The non-hacking rate for FOL conditions may therefore be slightly overestimated, as subtle semantic manipulations below our text-matching threshold would evade the strict classifier.

\subsection{H8 --- Premise-Subset Gaming}
\label{app:h8}

Manual audit of ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 revealed a previously undetected hacking mode: the model emits a subset of the gold premises that is individually necessary (high ISR) but insufficient for the intended derivation, with proof success depending on the conclusion already being embedded (H1-style).
We term this \textbf{H8 (premise-subset gaming)}: formalizations where each component is LOO-necessary but the premise set is a strict subset of what the NL problem requires, inflating ISR without faithful reasoning.

\paragraph{Detection.} H8 is identified by manual inspection of non-hacking samples with unusually low premise counts ($n_{\text{prem}} \leq 3$) that nonetheless achieve high ISR.
Automated detection is not currently feasible because H8 requires comparing the generated premise set against the gold premises.

\paragraph{Audit scope and limitations.}
Full H8 audit was completed for ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 only.
ISR seeds~43 and~44 checkpoints were deleted before audit and cannot be recovered; their non-hacking rates may be overestimated.
Random $\beta{=}0.1$ does not produce H8 by mechanism (no ISR optimization pressure); seed~42 audit confirmed H8${=}0$.

\paragraph{H7 false-negative correction (H7b obfuscated tautology).}
ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~44 contained 12 samples with $n_{\text{prem}}{=}1$ classified as non-hacking by the text matcher.
Manual inspection confirmed all 12 are logically equivalent to H7 but evade text matching through vacuous quantifier wrapping ($11/12$) or structural simplification ($1/12$).
We classify these as \textbf{H7b} (obfuscated tautology), distinct from text-match-detectable H7a.
$10/12$ achieve $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.83$, indicating simultaneous gaming of execution reward, ISR metric, and H7 classifier (triple gaming; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
After correction, ISR s44 non-hacking${=}0$; total H7 = H7a (77 text-match) + H7b (12 obfuscated) = 89.

\paragraph{Impact on non-hacking-rate comparison.}
After H8 reclassification and H7 false-negative correction: ISR non-hacking $= 14/231 = 6.06\%$ vs.\ random non-hacking $= 25/262 = 9.5\%$ (Fisher $p{=}0.182$, n.s.; Wilson 95\% CI: ISR [3.6\%, 9.9\%], Random [6.5\%, 13.7\%]).
The direction is consistent with ISR-amplified gaming modes (H7, H8) displacing non-hacking output, but the effect is not statistically significant at the conventional $\alpha{=}0.05$ threshold.

\subsection{H1 --- Conclusion Embedding}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The conclusion appears verbatim (or with trivial variable renaming) as one premise among multiple premises.
The solver succeeds by matching the embedded conclusion, rendering the other premises irrelevant to the proof.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x (bird(x) -> flies(x)).
  bird(tweety).
  flies(tweety).  % conclusion embedded
Conclusion: flies(tweety).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
Variable. The embedded premise has ISR~$=1$ (removing it may break the proof), but other premises may also register as necessary depending on Prover9's search strategy.
ISR does not distinguish trivial from substantive necessity.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Conclusion embedding in some form (H1 multi-premise or H7 single-premise) is GRPO-universal at 68--97\% across all RL conditions.
Under exec-only and Random reward, it manifests as H1 (59--91\%); under ISR reward, it shifts to H7 (54\% pooled, 5-seed).


\subsection{H7a --- Conclusion Duplication (Standard)}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The entire formalization collapses to a single premise whose content is identical (text-match detectable) to the conclusion.
Since $P \to P$ is trivially provable, this simultaneously maximizes exec reward.
Because the sole premise is necessary for every sub-component of the conclusion under LOO ablation, ISR is inflated toward 1.0.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
Conclusion:
  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0.8$--$1.0$.
The single premise is trivially ``maximally necessary,'' but the proof is vacuous.
H7a games both exec reward and ISR reward; H7b extends this to triple gaming by additionally evading the text-match classifier.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
H7a (text-match detectable): 64.5\% (149/231, 3-seed) under ISR~$\beta{=}0.1$ (s42: 16.0\%, s43: 96.7\%, s44: 86.5\%); 5-seed pooled H7: 54\% (190/350, Table~\ref{tab:goodhart-landscape}).
Combined H7 (H7a + H7b, 3-seed): 70.6\% (163/231; s43 H7a${=}59$ + H7b${=}2$; includes s44 FN correction).
Random~$\beta{=}0.1$ pooled: 29.5\% (122/414, 5-seed, all H7a; driven by s46 at 91.5\% and s43 at 38.3\%; s42/s44/s45 at 0\%).


\subsection{H7b --- Obfuscated Tautology}

\paragraph{Definition.}
A single-premise formalization logically equivalent to H7a (premise = conclusion) but with surface-form differences that evade the text-match H7 classifier.
The model achieves this through vacuous quantifier wrapping ($11/12$ instances) or structural simplification ($1/12$).

\paragraph{Example (FOL, vacuous quantifier wrapping).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x all y ((A(x)&B(y))->(C(x)|D(y))).
Conclusion:
  all x ((A(x)&B(x))->(C(x)|D(x))).
\end{verbatim}}
The premise introduces a vacuous second quantifier variable $y$ that is immediately unified with $x$, making the formulas logically equivalent while differing textually.

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
$\text{ISR}{\geq}0.83$ ($10/12$ samples).
H7b simultaneously games three objectives: execution reward ($r_{\text{exec}}{=}1$ via tautological proof), ISR metric (single necessary premise yields high ISR), and the text-match H7 classifier (surface-form difference evades detection).
This triple gaming makes H7b the most complete Goodhart case we observe.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Found primarily in ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~44 ($12/89$ proved samples, all originally classified as non-hacking); seed~43 contributes $2$ additional cases.
Functional cross-validation via $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$ exposed the misclassification.


\subsection{Tautological Collapse}

\paragraph{Definition.}
Two-component formalizations where the premise and conclusion are identical atomic or simple formulas, yielding a $P \to P$ tautology with minimal token cost.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
\begin{verbatim}
Premises: p(a).
Conclusion: p(a).
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$=1.0$ (the sole premise is necessary).
Distinguished from H7 by having low component count ($n_{\text{comp}}\approx 2$) and atomic formulas rather than complex sub-structured conclusions.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Dominant in FOL exec-only seed~44 (PR~$=0.98$, mean $n_{\text{comp}}=2.04$, 100\% H7 by strict classifier).
Also observed in Prolog exec+STA seed~42 (100\% H7, PR~$=0.50$).


\subsection{Repetition Collapse}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The model generates identical premises or clauses repeated until the maximum completion length, producing a degenerate output with high token count but no logical diversity.
Removing any single repeated copy leaves the others intact, yielding ISR~$\approx 0$.

\paragraph{Example (Prolog).}
\begin{verbatim}
penguin(fido).
penguin(fido).
penguin(fido).
... (repeated to 512 tokens)
query(penguin(fido)).
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0$. Each copy is individually redundant since identical copies remain after removal.
ISR correctly diagnoses this degeneration.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed in FOL exec-only seed~43 (87\% of outputs hit max completion length; PR~$=13$\%, ISR~$=0$).


\subsection{Complexity-without-Utility}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The formalization contains syntactically complex premises (nested quantifiers, multi-arity predicates) that are semantically vacuous; none is individually necessary for the proof.
The complexity inflates surface metrics (formula length, nesting depth) without contributing to logical derivation.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x all y (R(x,y) ->
    exists z (S(x,z) & T(z,y))).
  all x (P(x) -> Q(x)).
  P(a).            % only this needed
Conclusion: Q(a).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR correctly identifies the vacuous premises (ISR~$=0$ for each), pulling down the mean ISR.
This is the mode ISR is best calibrated for.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Low. Observed in Random~$\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 at 3.8\% (3/79).
Not observed under ISR reward (ISR's gradient discourages zero-ISR premises).


\subsection{Contradiction Explosion}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The component count grows unboundedly over training.
Excess premises introduce contradictions or redundancies that trivially entail any conclusion via \emph{ex falso quodlibet}.
Individual premises may register as ISR~$=0$ (removable without breaking the proof), but the sheer count obscures the underlying triviality.

\paragraph{Example (FOL, 1000-step exec-only).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  c1. c2. c3. ... c18. % 18.55 mean
  % conclusion embedded among premises
Conclusion: Q(a).
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0$ (at 1000 steps: ISR~$=0.003$, with 94.8\% of proved samples having ISR~$=0$).

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed in extended exec-only training (seed~42, 1000 steps).
Mean component count grows from ${\sim}6$ (500 steps) to 18.55 (1000 steps).


\subsection{Query-as-Fact Gaming}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The model converts the natural language conclusion into a snake\_case atom and includes it as both a ground fact and the query.
Prolog trivially proves the query by unifying with the fact.
This mode evades text-match classifiers designed for H1/H7 because the generated atom bears no surface resemblance to the original conclusion text.

\paragraph{Example (Prolog).}
\begin{verbatim}
% NL: "Fido is happy."
% Model output:
fido_is_happy.
:- fido_is_happy.     % query = fact
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$\approx 0.9$--$1.0$.
The single fact is trivially necessary (its removal breaks the query), inflating ISR.
Functionally equivalent to H7 but with a distinct surface mechanism.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed in Prolog exec+STA seed~44 (PR~$=0.97$, ISR~$=0.912$).
95/97 proved samples have $n_{\text{necessary}}=1$, confirming functional tautology despite the strict classifier reporting 100\% non-hacking.


\subsection{H9 --- Ex Falso Quodlibet (Contradiction Injection)}

\paragraph{Definition.}
The model generates a premise set containing logically contradictory assertions (e.g., $P(x)$ and $\neg P(x)$).
From contradictory premises, any conclusion follows by the \emph{ex falso quodlibet} principle, rendering the proof semantically vacuous regardless of the conclusion's content.
Unlike the ``contradiction explosion'' mode observed in 4B exec-only at 1000 steps (where contradictions arise incidentally among inflated premise counts), H9 is a \emph{targeted} strategy: the model constructs minimal contradictory pairs that directly enable the proof.

\paragraph{Example (FOL).}
{\small\begin{verbatim}
Premises:
  all x (bird(x) -> flies(x)).
  bird(tweety).
  -bird(tweety).  % contradicts above
Conclusion: happy(tweety).
% Proof: bird(tweety) & -bird(tweety) -> False -> anything
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{ISR interaction.}
ISR~$>0$ because each side of the contradiction is individually necessary under LOO: removing $P(x)$ leaves $\neg P(x)$ alone, which cannot derive a contradiction; removing $\neg P(x)$ leaves the premises consistent but insufficient to derive an unrelated conclusion.
The LOO test thus registers both contradictory premises as ``necessary,'' inflating ISR despite the formalization being semantically vacuous.

\paragraph{Prevalence.}
Observed exclusively in Qwen3-1.7B under Random $\beta{=}0.1$ (seed~42, 500 steps, proper train/eval separation): 100\% of proved samples ($n{=}93$) exhibit H9.
Under ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ with the same model, H9 does not appear; the model instead converges to fixed-template H1 ($\text{ISR}{=}0.6$, zero variance), indicating that ISR reward redirects the hacking pathway from H9 to H1.
Not observed in any Qwen3-4B experiment across all conditions and seeds tested. %% registry: d113-1.7b-random-b01-s42

and seed~44 converts NL conclusions to snake\_case atoms used as both fact and query.
The diversity of gaming pathways across seeds, despite identical training data and reward function, demonstrates that Goodhart's Law in neurosymbolic reasoning is not a single failure mode but a family of convergent exploits.

\subsection{Early-Training Hacking Analysis (100-Step Checkpoint)}
\label{app:100step}

To control for the prove-rate confound in our SFT comparison (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}), we analyze the exec-only checkpoint at 100 training steps (seed~42), where PR${=}32$\%, higher than SFT (13.0\%, 3-seed pooled) but still early in training.
Of the 32 proved samples, 9 (28.1\%) exhibit H7 hacking (single premise identical to conclusion) and 1 (3.1\%) exhibits H1 (conclusion embedded among premises), yielding a total hacking rate of 31.2\%.
By contrast, SFT at comparable or lower PR shows 7.7\% hacking (1/13 proved samples).
This demonstrates that reward hacking emerges early in GRPO training, well before the prove-rate plateau, and is not simply an artifact of having more proved samples available for exploitation.
The 100-step hacking rate (31.2\%) is already substantially above SFT (7.7\%), supporting the claim that hacking is associated with RL optimization rather than prove-rate level alone.

\subsection{$O(1)$ vs.\ $O(n)$ ISR Ablation}
\label{app:o1-ablation}

To justify the per-clause LOO design (\S\ref{sec:sta}), we train a variant that replaces the $O(n)$ ablation with a cheaper $O(1)$ binary signal: $\text{fast\_ISR}(x) = 1$ if $x$ is proved \emph{and} the conclusion is not provable under empty premises (tautology check), $0$ otherwise.
The reward becomes $r = 0.5\,r_{\text{exec}} + 0.5\,\text{fast\_ISR}$.
After 500 steps (seed~42), this variant achieves $\text{PR}{=}63\%$ with $\text{ISR}^*{=}0.007$ (functionally zero), compared to $\text{ISR}^*{=}0.132$ under standard exec-only and $\text{ISR}^*{=}0.42$ under ISR $\beta{=}0.1$.

\paragraph{ISR signal vs.\ training dynamics.}
At the \emph{ISR signal level}, the $O(1)$ variant is indistinguishable from exec-only: both produce near-zero ISR because models emit redundant premise copies whose individual removal never changes the proof outcome.
At the \emph{training level}, the two conditions are non-equivalent: the $O(1)$ tautology check penalizes formalizations where the conclusion is provable without any premises, a constraint absent from exec-only.
This confound depresses prove rate by 30 percentage points ($63\%$ vs.\ $93\%$ exec-only), making it impossible to attribute the difference purely to the ISR signal.
The result confirms that the $O(n)$ per-clause ablation is necessary for ISR to carry a structural signal, while also showing that even a minimal tautology guard alters training dynamics substantially.
